children: Oil prices whipsawed in early trading after a report said Iran has offered to reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz shipping route within seven days if the U.S. takes initial steps toward easing military pressure.

Crude prices had fallen for four straight days coming into Tuesday trading and were rebounding early on as traders saw lingering risks in the Middle East as fighting by Houthi rebels in Saudi Arabia intensified. But after the positive words from Tehran, Brent crude, the international benchmark dropped below the key $100 level-falling 0.5% to $99.75. West Texas Intermediate, the U.S. benchmark, also dropped-down 2% to $93.80.

"There is a possibility of moving toward an agreement," Japan's Kyodo News reported a senior Iranian government official as saying, while adding that Washington must demonstrate "seriousness and commitment" if diplomacy is to advance.
The proposal has already been conveyed to Washington through mediators, the report said. It calls for renewed talks aimed at reaching a permanent end to hostilities between the two countries.
Tehran plans to use the U.N. General Assembly gathering this week in New York to consult with countries acting as intermediaries with the U.S. to end the fighting, which began on Feb. 28.
